scope_note: Orange County is an area of many cities, not one city. The California codes apply everywhere; each city's building department issues permits and may adopt local amendments, and OC Public Works does so in unincorporated areas. The two largest cities, Anaheim and Santa Ana, were researched. Irvine and Huntington Beach are named on the page as further examples; their codes were not researched.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Orange County job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Orange County hotels, offices, schools and medical buildings, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** California's rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and they apply in every Orange County city. Anaheim adopts the counts unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** permits come from your own city's building department: Anaheim, Santa Ana, Irvine, Huntington Beach and the other cities each have one, and OC Public Works covers unincorporated areas. Anaheim and Santa Ana follow California's list of work that needs no permit. It covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work" and movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask your city's building department whether your replacement needs one. In Santa Ana that is the Building Safety Division, (714) 647-5800. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: California counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. A city can add to the state's rules, so your own city's building department has the final word.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or your city's building department sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Each Orange County city sets its own business license and permit steps. In Santa Ana, for example, a contractor who takes out a permit needs a city business license. In unincorporated areas the county sets no contractor license of its own. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Orange County the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Orange County that is $54.41 an hour plus $29.91 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.75% in most of Orange County, including Anaheim, Irvine and Huntington Beach: 7.25% statewide and 0.5% for the county transportation authority. Santa Ana adds 1.5% of its own, for 9.25%; its city tax drops to 1% on April 1, 2029. Ten other cities add 1% or 1.5%, so check the rate for your delivery address.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, resorts and convention venues:** stainless steel or phenolic with extra privacy options for busy guest restrooms.
